raw_response.publication_year_note: The cached 19-page PDF is an unformatted author manuscript/postprint with no journal header, volume/issue, copyright line, or publication year printed anywhere on the document. The latest dates printed in the reference list are 'accepted on 22 December 2014' (p. 16) and URL access dates of '02 January 2015' and '11 February 2015' (pp. 17, 19).
raw_response.rationale: This methodological case study in San Sebastián de Yalí, Nicaragua develops a stratified household sampling protocol (households served by CAPS community water committees vs. informal self-provision; n = 107 polled out of N = 296 households across 5 rural communities) and 0-to-1 composite indicators across five human-right-to-water dimensions. While finite-population Clopper-Pearson binomial error bounds are used ex ante to set target sample sizes (alpha = 0.90, e < 0.20; overall sample e = 0.11-0.13, pp. 7-8), the empirical comparison of CAPS-served vs. self-provided households reports only unquantified graphical spider charts (Figures 2-4) and descriptive faecal-coliform percentages (64%, 20% and 16% for self-provided vs. 0%, 82% and 18% for CAPS-served, p. 9), with zero inferential tests, regression models, standard errors, confidence intervals on group contrasts, or p-values, and explicitly states that uncertainty analysis of the composite indicators is beyond the scope of the article (p. 6).
